questions.question: Acid changes the colour of blue litmus to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Acid**

 
 
• **​****Acid **changes the colour of blue litmus to **Red**.
 
• A **Brnsted-Lowry** acid or Lewis acid is a molecule or ion that can either donate a proton (the hydrogen ion, H+) or establish a covalent bond with an electron pair. **Proton** donors, also known as** Brnsted-Lowry acids**, are the first class of **acids**.
 
• Proton donors, also referred to as Arrhenius acids, generate the hydronium ion** H3O+** under the unique situation of aqueous solutions.
 
• The **Arrhenius **theory was expanded upon by Brnsted and Lowry to take non-aqueous solvents into account.
 
• A **hydrogen atom **is typically bound to a **chemical **structure in a **Brnsted **or **Arrhenius acid** that is still energetically advantageous after the loss of **H+**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aqueous** **Arrhenius** **acids** have distinguishing characteristics that serve as a useful definition of an **acid**. Acids can turn **blue litmus red**, produce aqueous solutions with a sour taste, and react with bases and some metals (like calcium) to generate salts.
 
• The Latin word **acidus**, which means **"sour,"** is where the word acid comes from. While the technical definition solely refers to the solute, an aqueous solution of an acid with a pH lower than 7 is sometimes commonly referred to as "acid" (as in **"dissolved in acid".**.
 
• Higher **acidity **and, thus, a higher concentration of **positive hydrogen **ions in the solution are indicative of a **lower pH**.

• "The** Jawadhi range**, in contrast to the Barahmahal hills to the **west**, is covered in vegetation all the way up to its **highest **point. As **dusk **falls, the entire range takes on a purple hue resembling a **heather** bloom.

questions.question: Under the Constitution of India, the Constitutional Head of the Executive of the Union is the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **President**

 
 
• The **head** of **state **of the** Republic of India** is the **president**.
 
• The **president **serves as the **titular **leader of the executive branch, the nation's first **citizen**, and the **supreme commander** of the Indian** Armed Forces.**
 
• The **15th **and current president is **Droupadi Murmu**, who took office on **July 25, 2022**.
 
• The position of **president **was established on **January 26, 1950**, when India became a republic after obtaining independence on August 15, 1947, when its **constitution **took effect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **legislative **assemblies of each of India's states and **territories**, as well as both **chambers **of the **Indian Parliament,** which were all chosen directly by the people, are used to elect the president in an indirect manner.
 
• With a few exceptions, **Article 53** of the** Indian Constitution** states that the president may exercise their powers directly or through a subordinate authority.
 
• In practise, however, the **prime minister **a subordinate authority exercises all of the **president's **executive powers while receiving advice from the **Cabinet Ministers**.

• Awarded for "distinguished achievement in different realms of life, including the **arts**, **education**, **industry**, **literature**, **research**, **acting**, **medicine**, **social service**, and public affairs," the award was established on **January 2, 1954**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the recognition of the right to education as a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 21 A.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 21 A**

 
 
• **Article 21-A,** which states that all children between the ages of **six **and **fourteen **have the fundamental right to free and compulsory education, was added to the **Indian Constitution** by the **Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act of 2002**.
 
• Every child has the right to a full-time **elementary education **of satisfactory and **equitable **quality in a formal school that complies with certain **fundamental **norms and standards.
 
• According to the** Right of Children** to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE)** Act, 2009**, which represents the consequential legislation anticipated under** Article 21-A**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** RTE Act **and** Article 21-A** both went into force on **April 1, 2010**.
 
• The words **"free and compulsory" **are part of the **RTE **Act's title. Under the definition of** "free education,"** no child aside from a child whose parents have allowed him or her to enrol in a school that is not financially supported by the relevant government shall be required to pay any kind of **fee**, **charge**, or expense that might prevent them from pursuing and completing **elementary **education.

questions.question: During the period between 1950 and 1990, the proportion of GDP contributed by agriculture significantly ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Declined**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, the share of agriculture in the country's **GDP decreased **dramatically between 1950 and 1990 (from 67.5% to 64.9%), but not the population that depended on it.
 
• **​**A monetary indicator of the market worth of all the final goods and services produced and sold (not resold) in a certain time period by nations is the **gross domestic product (GDP)**.
 
• This measurement is frequently reviewed before being regarded as a valid indicator due to its subjective and complicated character. While nominal **GDP** is more useful for comparing **national economies** on the **global market**.
 
• **GDP **(nominal) per capita does not account for variations in the cost of living and **inflation rates **of the various nations.
 
• The contribution made by each **industry **or **sector** of the economy can also be calculated as a **percentage **of the total **GDP**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Many national and **international** economic groups keep track of **GDP **definitions.
 
• The **GDP **is defined by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development** (OECD)** as "an aggregate measure of production equal to the sum of the gross values added of all resident and institutional units engaged in production and services (plus any taxes, and minus any subsidies on products not **included **in the value of their outputs)".
 
• According to an **IMF **report, "**GDP** represents the monetary value of final goods and services that are purchased by the final user **produced **in a country in a certain period of **time **(say, a quarter or a year)."

questions.question: What is the product of a reaction of calcium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium hydrogen carbonate**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calcium hydrogen carbonate**

 
 
• **​Ca(HCO3)2** is the chemical formula for **calcium bicarbonate**, often known as **calcium hydrogencarbonate**.
 
• It only exists in aqueous solutions containing calcium **(Ca2+)**, bicarbonate ions, and dissolved carbon dioxide; the word does not refer to a known solid substance** (CO2)**.
 
• The **pH **affects the relative quantities of these **carbon-containing species**, with **bicarbonate **predominating in fresh water between **6.36 **and **10.25**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The majority of **natural waters **that are drawn from **streams**, **lakes**, and especially **wells** can be thought of as **diluted **solutions of these **bicarbonates **because all waters that come into contact with the **atmosphere **absorb **carbon dioxide**.
 
• As these waters interact with rocks and **sediments **they pick up metal ions, most frequently **calcium** and **magnesium**.
 
• These hard **fluids **often result in **carbonate **scale building up in boilers and **pipes**, and when they interact with **soap**, they create an unfavourable **scum**.

questions.question: Fa Xian began his journey back home from which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Bengal.__**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fa Xian** boarded a ship owned by some merchants to start his voyage back home from **Bengal**.
 
• **​****Faxian **was a Chinese **Buddhist** monk and translator who walked on foot from **China **to **India **in search of Buddhist literature.
 
• He was also known by the names **Fa-Hien**,** Fa-hsien**, and **Sehi**.
 
• **Between 399** and **412 CE**, he began his gruelling journey at the age of roughly **60**, visiting holy **Buddhist **places in **Central**, **South**, and **Southeast Asia**, with 10 of those years spent in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihar**

 
 
• **​Eastern **India contains the state of **Bihar**.
 
• It is the second most populous state in terms of people in 2019, has the 12th-largest size (94,163 km2) and the 14th-largest GDP in 2021.
 
• **Bihar **shares borders with **Jharkhand **to the **south**, **Uttar Pradesh** to the **west**, **Nepal **to the **north**, and the **northern **portion of **West Bengal** to the **east**.
 
• The **Ganges **River, which runs from **west **to **east**, divides the** Bihar plain**.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**
 
 
• ​**Maharashtra** is a state in western India's peninsula that takes up a sizable chunk of the** Deccan Plateau**. **Maharashtra** is the second-most populous country subdivision in the world as well as the second-most populous state in India.
 
• The bilingual **Bombay** **State**, which had been in existence since 1956, was divided on May 1 to create the majority-**Marathi-speaking Maharashtra** and the majority-**Gujarati-speaking Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**
 
 
• **Eastern** **India** is home to the Indian state of **Odisha**. By area, it is the eighth-largest state, and by population, it is the eleventh-largest. The number of scheduled tribes in the state is the third highest in all of **India**.
 
• It shares borders with the states of Andhra Pradesh to the south, Jharkhand to the north, West Bengal to the northeast, and Chhattisgarh to the west. Odisha's coastline stretches for 485 kilometres (301 mi) along the Indian Ocean's Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Gross primary deficit can be expressed as ________.

options.text: Gross fiscal deficit - Net interest liabilities
Gross fiscal deficit + Net interest liabilities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is G__**ross fiscal deficit - Net interest liabilities**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primary Deficit**

 
 
• **​​**The difference between the **fiscal** **deficit **for the current fiscal year and the interest **payment **required for the prior fiscal year is referred to as the **primary deficit**.
 
• It is one of the three **crucial metrics** for calculating the **federal defici**t.
 
• It displays the **government's **borrowing needs but does not include interest of any kind. In addition to the** interest payment**.
 
• It draws attention to the total amount of **government **spending that must be covered by borrowing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary deficit** is the difference between total government borrowings and interest **payments**, or fiscal deficit, and total **government **borrowings only.
 
• In most cases, when a **loan **is raised by the **government**, the **interest **payment **amount** is also included.
 
• When the principal loan amount is removed from this **sum**, the **primary deficit **is shown.

questions.question: The news print sector in our country is governed by which order from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newsprint Control Order, 2004.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The 1955 **Essential Commodities Act** covered newsprint. The **Newsprint Control Order of 1962** controlled its production and trade.
 
• The **Newsprint Control Order** was revoked in 2004 and **Newsprint** was removed from the list of essential goods.
 
• The** Newsprint Control Order 2004** was then published in its place. This enables the mills that produce newspapers to register with** Schedule I**. Subject to the actual user condition, mills registered under the schedule are exempt from excise duty. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Newsprint 

 
 
• ​Newspapers, other periodicals, and advertising materials are most frequently printed on newsprint, a cheap, non-archival paper made primarily of wood pulp.
 
• It was created in 1844 by Charles Fenerty in Nova Scotia, Canada, and often has an off-white cast.
 
• It is made to be used in printing presses that use large webs of paper rather than single sheets of paper, such as web offset, letterpress, and flexographic.
 
• Publishers and printers prefer newsprint because it is relatively inexpensive (in comparison to paper grades used for glossy magazines and sales brochures), sturdy (enough to run through contemporary high-speed web printing presses), and can accept four-color printing at qualities suitable for standard newspapers.

questions.question: Which element of group 13 is a soft metal with a low melting point (303K) and is widely used in doping semiconductors and producing solid-state devices such as transistors?
questions.solution:

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gallium**

 
 
• **​**The chemical element **gallium **has the atomic number **31** and the symbol **Ga**.
 
• Gallium is a metal in group 13 of the periodic table and was first discovered by the French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran in 1875. (**aluminium**, **indium**, and **thallium**).
 
• **Gallium **is an **element **that is **soft **and **silvery** at ordinary **pressure **and** temperature**.
 
• It turns **silvery **white when it's liquid. **Gallium **may fracture **conchoidally **if excessive force is used.
 
• **Gallium** has been** **commonly **utilised **to create **alloys** with low melting points ever since it was discovered in **1875**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chemical element **aluminium **has the atomic number **13 **and the symbol **Al**. **Aluminum **has a density that is around one third that of **steel**, which is lower than that of most common **metals**.
 
• Chemical element **boron** has the atomic number **5 **and the letter B in its symbol. It is an **amorphous **brown powder and a brittle, black, glossy metalloid in its **crystalline **form.
 
• The chemical element **thalium **has the atomic number **81 **and the letter **Tl **assigned to it. It is a** post-transition** grey metal that is not naturally occurring in free form. while **segregated**.

questions.question: What type of isomerism exists in compounds containing two or more complexes, each of which contains a different set of ligands that can in principle be replaced with a ligand of the other complex?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coordination isomerism.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coordination isomerism**

 
 
• **​**A type of structural **isomerism **known as** coordination isomerism** occurs when the coordination** complex ion'**s makeup changes.
 
• The overall **ligand **to metal ratio in a **coordination isomer **doesn't vary, but the **ligands **bound to a particular **metal **ion do.
 
• Instances of a whole series of **coordination** **isomers **call for two or even more** metal ions**.
 
• The **exchange **of one or more ligands between the cationic complex ion and the anionic complex ion is known as coordination isomerism, and it happens in **compounds **that have** complex anionic** and **cationic components**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Two or more **coordination compounds **having a difference in composition within the **coordination **sphere are said to be **coordination isomers**.
 
• This kind of **isomerism **is caused by the exchange of **ligands **between anionic and cationic entities of various metal ions that are present in the complex.
 
• **Coordination isomerism**, which can be thought of as an exchange of some **ligands **from the **cation **to the anion, occurs in **compounds **that contain complex cationic and **anionic components**.
 
• As a result, two **complicated chemicals **that have opposite charges one **negative **and the other **positive **are linked together.

questions.question: Which of the following rocks is formed by the cooling and crystallisation of magma?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Granite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On all continents, **granitic rocks** can be found close to or past plate borders.
 
• They developed as **magma** **cooled thousands of kilometres below the surface of the Earth.**
 
• Then, as the** volcanic mountains** above them eroded away, the **granitic rocks** were elevated to the surface.
 
• **Granitic rocks**, which were cooled from rock melted during the subduction process that also created the **Franciscan Complex's rocks**, make up the **Sierra Nevada's core in California.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magma**

 
 
• All **igneous rocks **are formed from **magma**, which is a naturally occurring substance that is molten or semi-molten.
 
• The **Earth** possesses **magma** beneath its surface, and other terrestrial planets and several naturally occurring satellites have also been confirmed to have magmatic activity.
 
• **Magma** may also include gas bubbles and suspended crystals in addition to molten rock.
 
• In a variety o**f tectonic settings on Earth,** including as subduction **zones**, continental rift **zones**, mid-ocean ridges, and hotspots, the **mantle** or the **crust** melts to produce **magma**.
 
• **Mantle and crustal melts** are assumed to be stored in **magma** **chambers** **or trans-crustal crystal-rich **mush zones as they move upward through the **crust**.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities is an exponent of Kathak dance in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prerna Shrimali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Senior** Kathak dancer** of the **Jaipur Gharana is Prerana Shrimali**.
 
• **Shrimati Prerana Shrimali,** who was born in **Banswara, Rajasthan**, was trained in **Kathak dancing by Guru Shri Kundan lal Gangani in Jaipur**. Subsequently, she received instruction in the art from the same **Guru, late Shri Kundan Lal Gangani **of the **Jaipur gharana**, at **Kathak Kendra in New Delhi.**
 
• She has also taken part in numerous international dance seminars and conferences and created a number of performances.
 
• Also, she has trained young dancers at **Shriram Bharatiya Kala Kendra and Gandharva Mahavidyalaya.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak dance**

 
 
• ​One of the eight primary styles of Indian classical dance is **kathak**.
 
• It is an **Uttar Pradesh** classical dancing style. The storytellers or itinerant bards known as **Kathakars** in **ancient northern India** are often credited as the creators of **Kathak**.
 
• The **Vedic Sanskrit words Katha**, which means "story," and **Kathakar**, which means "the one who tells a story" or "to do with stories," are the roots of the word **Kathak**.
 
• Traveling **Kathakars** used dance, songs, and music to transmit tales from the great epics and ancient mythology. **Kathak dancers** use intricate footwork, flexible body movements, and, most importantly, expressive face expressions to convey a variety of stories.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) in May 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nidhi Chibber.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nidhi Chibber, a senior IAS officer**, was appointed to lead the **Central Board of Secondary Education** in May 2022 (**CBSE**).
 
• A member of the **Indian Administrative Service is Nidhi Chhibber.**
 
• **Nidhi Chibber,** an** Indian Administrative Service **officer from the 1994 batch assigned to the **Chhattisgarh** cadre, has been appointed as the new head of the **Central Board of Secondary Education.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Board of Secondary Education**

 
 
• The **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)** is the **government of India's national board of secondary education **for both** public and private schools.**
 
• The **Board** was a government-instituted experiment in interstate integration and collaboration in secondary education that was established in 1929.
 
• The **CBSE** is associated with more than 27,000 schools in India and 240 schools in 28 other countries.
 
• The **NCERT** curriculum is utilised by all **CBSE-affiliated institutions**, particularly in grades 9 through 12.
 
• **Nidhi Chibber, an IAS, is the CBSE's current chairwoman.**

questions.question: Which of the following Gharanas does Padma Bhushan Kishori Amonkar belong to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaipur-Atrauli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kishori Amonkar** was an inventive representative of the **Jaipur Gharana** and one of the greatest singers in the Indian classical vocal heritage.
 
• Indian classical dancer, choreographer, and teacher **Mrinalini Vikram Sarabhai.**
 
• Indian classical vocalist **Mogubai Kurdikar, **who lived from July 15, 1904, until February 10, 2001, was a well-known member of the** Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana.**
 
• **Madurai Shanmukhavadivu Subbulakshmi**, often known as **MS Subbulakshmi,** was a **Tamil Nadu-born Indian Carnatic **singer. She was the first musician ever to receive India's highest civilian distinction, the **Bharat Ratna.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jaipur Gharana**

 
 
• **​**The **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana **developed from the family of **Alladiya Khan**, who came from **Atrauli** and settled in **Jaipur**.
 
• **Alladiya Khan** (1855–1946), a pioneer of** Hindustani music**, developed the **Jaipur–Atrauli Gharana.**
 
• The raga repertory, vocal aesthetics, and technical prowess of the **Gharana **are well renowned.
 
• **Alladiya Khan, Mallikarjun Mansur, Kesarbhai Kerkar, Kishori Amonkar, Shruti Sadolikar, Padma Talwalkar**, and** Ashwini Bhide Deshpande** are the leading representatives of the **Jaipur Gharana.**

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of Visva-Bharati University?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At** Santiniketan, West Bengal, India**, it is a public research **university** and an **Institute of National **Importance.
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** formed it in 1921 and gave it the name **Visva-Bharati,** which translates to "the communion of the world with India."
 
• It was a college up till **independence**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath** **Tagore**

 
 
• **Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore,** a **Bengali** **polymath** who was a poet, playwright, novelist, composer, philosopher, social reformer, and painter, lived from 7 May 1861 to 7 August 1941.
 
• In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, he used contextual modernism to transform Indian art, Bengali literature, and music.
 
• **Gitanjali**, whose poetry has been described as "profoundly sensitive, fresh, and lovely," was the first **non-European** and lyricist to win the** Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.**
 
• **Tagore's **"beautiful prose and mystical poetry" are largely unknown outside of **Bengal**, despite the fact that his poetic songs were considered to be spiritual and mercurial. He was a **Royal Asiatic Society** fellow.
 
• **Tagore** was referred regarded as **"the Bard of Bengal"** and went by the nicknames **Gurudeb, Kobiguru, and Biswokobi. **

• ​For both students and** Assamese citizens**, a caste certificate is a necessary document. Prior to now, obtaining a caste certificate required individuals to go to the appropriate government office.
 
• **Mission Bhumiputra** is a new platform that the **Hon**. **Chief Minister of Assam, Dr Himanta Biswa Sharma,** has introduced for the online application of caste certificates in **Assam**.
 
• An online platform called **Assam Mission Bhumiputra **was created to make it easier and quicker for residents to get caste certificates directly.
 
• When applying for certain** government employment, government programmes,** or admittance to schools and colleges, these cast certifications could be necessary.
 
• The entire procedure for applying for a caste certificate online through the **Mission Bhumiputra portal** is outlined here.

questions.question: In the ________, Sarojini Naidu persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to allow women to join the movement.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt Satyagraha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian political activist, feminist, **and** poet Sarojini Naidu **(13 February 1879 – 2 March 1949) was born in India.
 
• She played a significant role in **India's fight for independence** from colonial control as a supporter of **civil rights**, **women's emancipation, **and** anti-imperialist beliefs.**
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** was convinced by **Sarojini Naidu **to permit women to participate in the **Dandi March**.
 
• She was also the first **Indian** woman to be selected as **governor of an Indian state** and to serve as **president** of the **Indian National Congress (United Provinces).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salt Satyagraha**

 
 
• ​**Mahatma Gandhi** led the **nonviolent civil disobedience movement** known as the** Salt March,** sometimes referred to as the **Salt Satyagraha**, the **Dandi March**, and the** Dandi Satyagraha**, in colonial India.
 
• The 24-day march, which served as a direct-action campaign of tax resistance and peaceful protest against the** British salt monopoly,** took place from March 12 to April 6, 1930.
 
• The **Civil Disobedience Movement **need a powerful inauguration to encourage more people to follow **Gandhi's** example, which was another motivation for this march.
 
• **Gandhi **led 78 of his dependable volunteers at the beginning of this march.
 
• The march covered a distance of **387 km (240 mi)**, from **Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi**, which was then known as **Navsari** (now in the state of Gujarat).

__
 
• The **World Para Athletics Grand Prix** got underway on March 21 and last until March 24, 2022. This occasion took place in **Dubai**.
 
• There will be **450 competitors** competing from **43 different nations.**
 
• The competitors competing in this event aim to qualify for both the **Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games** and the **Hangzhou 2022 Asian Para Games**.
 
• **Over 100 para-athletes**, including Indian participants, have the chance to get classified in this event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Para Athletics Championship**

 
 
• ​The** International Paralympic Committee's World Para Athletics** subcommittee hosts the biennial **World Para Athletics Championships**, formerly known as the **IPC Athletics World Championships before 2017 (IPC).**
 
• Athletes with intellectual and physical limitations compete in sporting competitions.
 
• **Berlin, Germany **hosted the inaugural **IPC Athletics World Championships in 1994**.
 
• They serve as a **Paralympic** equivalent of the able-bodied competitors' **World Athletics Championships.**
 
• The **IPC championships** have been conducted in the same years as the** IAAF championships** since 2011 when they changed from a quadrennial to a biennial calendar. However, they are independent competitions, and they are not always held in the same host city.

questions.question: Which of the following players is associated with badminton?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Srikanth Kidambi** is an **Indian badminton player **who was born on 7 February 1993.
 
• **Kidambi**, a former world number one, received the **Arjuna award in 2015** and the **Padma Shri, **India's fourth-highest civilian honour, in 2018.
 
• He was the first Indian to play in the men's singles final of a** World Championship in 2021.**

• **Badminton**

 
 
• **Racquets** are used in the racquet sport of **badminton** to hit a **shuttlecock** through a net.
 
• The most popular versions of the game are "singles" (with one player per side) and "doubles," however it can also be played with bigger teams (with two players per side).
 
• While formal matches are conducted on a rectangular indoor court, **badminton** is frequently played as a recreational outdoor pastime in a yard or on a beach.
 
• The **shuttlecock** must land in the half of the court belonging to the opposing team in order to score a point.​

questions.question: Subsidiary alliance treaty was imposed on Awadh in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1801**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nawab of Awadh** was forced to accept the **Policy of Subsidiary Alliance by Wellesley in 1801.**
 
• The first king to form a secondary alliance with the **British** following the **Battle of Buxar** was the **Nawab of Awadh**.
 
• The **Nizam of Hyderabad** was the first to consent to a carefully crafted **subsidiary alliance**, though.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Subsidiary Alliance**

 
 
• ​The **Subsidiary Alliance** was essentially a pact between the **British East India Company** and the princely states of India, through which the English gained control over the **Indian kingdoms.**
 
• It was also a significant factor in the development of the** British Empire in India.**
 
• **Lord Wellesley**, who served as the **Governor-General of India from 1798 to 1805,** drafted it.
 
• The** Marquis Dupleix**, the **French Governor-General**, really used it for the first time.
